newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end up, may test record next week.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end up, may test record next week.

text.p: South African stocks ended up on Friday as positive sentiment returned to the market when Wall Street was reassured by potentially inflation-sensitive data and went on to post opening gains, dealers said.

U.S. retail sales and September producer prices confirmed moderate growth with inflation under control for the U.S. economy. The Dow strengthened and dispelled dealers' fears that it would correct and drag South African markets down with it.
Trading was brisk and volumes heavy with strong international interest in South African blue-chip shares, dealers said.
The all-share index ended up 23 points to 7,054.5 as industrials jumped 31.7 points to 8,270.4.
Dealers said the all-share index could be gearing up to test its record life high of 7,086.8 next week. The record was set on April 26 earlier this year.

But some dealers cautioned that it would depend on the performance of the Dow, which had been threatening -- and failing -- to decisively break through the psychologically important 6,000 barrier for some time.
"All eyes will be on Wall Street," one dealer said.
Gold shares slipped on bullion fears and also the failure of the silver price to test the $5.10 level. The golds index fell back 11.8 points to 1,728.2.
But dealers said the gold quarterly figures due out next week from a host of mines and firms could boost sentiment in the sector.
